body:
## Why
`not ok 95 - a token inside the window is reported to the loop with the fix` failed on a UTC Actions runner (PR #47's run) while passing locally (EDT) and on main's next run. A test of a 7-day expiry window that depends on the process clock or timezone is a latent flake that will eventually fail main at random and erode trust in the CI gate.

## What
- Make the expiry logic in `src/doctor.js` take an injectable `now` (default `Date.now`), same pattern the reap/track code uses.
- The tests construct explicit instants (e.g. expiry = now + 6d23h, now + 7d1h, expired) instead of deriving from the real clock; run the boundary cases in both directions.
- While there: assert the warning text renders the date in UTC so the same token warns on the same day everywhere.

## Done when
`TZ=UTC node --test test/doctor.test.js` and `TZ=America/New_York node --test test/doctor.test.js` both pass at any wall-clock time (add both TZ runs to the test workflow's matrix if cheap).
title: Deterministic clock in the doctor expiry tests
